clue.text: All around expert player come to criticise

indicators.note: around tells us one piece wraps the other, with the phrase for arriving on the outside

parts.note: to come to a place is to reach it
an expert player is a professional, a pro

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a top performer from every angle on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All' reads as part of the definition but is only a link word; 'around' signals the container, and 'come to' is a verb meaning arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke or find fault with them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Officially reported second river had gone and changed channels

indicators.note: had gone means this letter has left the word

parts.note: a returning officer has returned the result when it is officially reported
R is the abbreviation for river; here it is the second R in the word

explanation.surface: A clerk notes that a second river had disappeared and its course moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second R out of RETURNED leaves the answer. Retuning a radio or TV changes the channel it receives.
explanation.definitionFit: To retune a set is to adjust it to a different frequency, so to change channels.

clue.text: Good time had in part of theatre

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed an evening in one section of a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The pit is the area in front of the stage, where the orchestra or cheap seats are.

clue.text: Terrible summer noted by Puccini?

parts.note: an ironic reading: a bad summer might have a single good day, and the phrase is a famous aria Puccini set to music

explanation.definitionFit: Un bel di, known in English by this phrase, is the soprano aria in Madama Butterfly by Puccini.

clue.text: Become friendly with sort of beetle? One can with mouse, too

definitions.meaning: two people who hit it off immediately are said to get on at once
a beetle that springs up with a snapping sound when on its back
pressing the button on a computer mouse does this

explanation.definitionFit: People hit it off, an insect named for its snapping noise, and pressing a computer mouse button all share this word.

clue.text: Stop talking and die — not in bed

parts.note: to hang is to die on the gallows
someone up is out of bed

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to fall silent, expire and get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang up is to end a phone call, so to stop talking to the other party.

clue.text: What one finds hard to take for long?

definitions.text: What one finds hard to take
definitions.meaning: a persistent pain is hard to bear
to yearn for something, as in a heart that pines

explanation.definitionFit: A dull pain is hard to bear, and to ache for something is to long for it.

clue.text: Arsonist's deed may come to nothing

definitions.meaning: what a fire-raiser makes a building do: burn away
plans that fail completely and vanish

explanation.definitionFit: Literally burning away, and figuratively vanishing without result, which is the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Old tribesman drinks wine, to act as oracle

indicators.note: drinks means the tribesman takes the wine inside him

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland
red is wine

explanation.surface: An ancient warrior downs some wine before foretelling the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks' is the container signal: the ancient Scot takes the wine inside. The Picts are a crossword favourite for old tribesmen.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle foretells events, so to act as one is to forecast what will happen.

clue.text: In wrong pitch, person representing sounds

indicators.note: In tells us the person goes inside the jumbled letters
wrong means these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one does one's best'

explanation.surface: A singer is off key, someone remarks about the sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles the letters of pitch into PHTIC, which 'In' then splits around the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetic spelling or script represents speech sounds, so the adjective means representing sounds.

clue.text: Pieces of Eliot she thought novel in the twenties

indicators.note: the words are broken into pieces and the letters reassembled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fragments of T. S. Eliot's ideas turn up in a book from the 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of ELIOT SHE THOUGHT rearrange into the title; the surface's mention of Eliot points away from the author, Virginia Woolf.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's novel of this title was published in 1927, so it is a twenties novel.

clue.text: Having no great objections to egg-collecting

definitions.meaning: making only petty, trivial objections, quibbling
nits are the eggs of lice, so picking them out is collecting eggs

explanation.definitionFit: Petty fault-finding is the usual sense, and literally the word means picking lice eggs from hair.

clue.text: After drunk turns up on beach, go off to rest uneasily

indicators.note: in a down entry turns up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sot is a drunk
sand stands for a beach
milk that goes off turns sour

explanation.surface: A drunk washes up on the shore and sleeps badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' is the reversal signal, apt in a down entry; 'After' and 'on' only set the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss and turn is to move restlessly in bed unable to sleep, an idiom.

clue.text: Musical performance I attended

parts.note: a gig is a live musical performance

explanation.surface: A concert-goer reports going to a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerner and Loewe's stage and film musical has this one-word title, so it is an example.

clue.text: Loved one's not up in town

parts.note: a darling is a loved one; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is absent from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NOT to TON. Darlington is a town in County Durham in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlington is a market town in north-east England, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Exaggerate being tricked about gun

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for cheated goes round the weapon

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them; did is the past tense
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Overstating the danger after being fooled about a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'being' is a link word. A Sten is a cheap British wartime submachine gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or inflate, so to make something larger than it is, to exaggerate.

clue.text: Not looking forward to daughter going to university?

parts.note: Reading is an English town with a university

explanation.surface: A parent dreads a daughter leaving home for college.
explanation.walkthrough: D plus READING, the English university town west of London; the surface's going to university hides the town name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreading something means anticipating it with fear, the opposite of looking forward to it.

clue.text: Players cooperating in characteristic passage

indicators.note: in places the players inside the word for a feature

parts.note: a characteristic is a trait
in bridge North and South are partners playing together

explanation.surface: Team-mates working together on a typical stretch of road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NS inside TRAIT. North and South are bridge partners, a crossword convention for cooperating players.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage from one place to another, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Calm position at inside

indicators.note: inside means the little word goes within the word for a spot

parts.note: a position is a place

explanation.surface: A tranquil spot has a little word tucked within it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal; 'at' is used as it stands, and 'position' looks like the definition but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to calm or pacify them, a direct synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Moved fast to distribute money round church

indicators.note: round means the money word wraps around the church abbreviation

parts.note: the pound is British money
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to hand out cash around the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal; 'to distribute' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat that pounced sprang suddenly on its prey, so it moved fast.

clue.text: Not feeling one can run rings round university

annotationWithheld.why: Not feeling one can run rings round university (7): CALLOUS reads as CALLS (rings) round OU (university), but 'one can run' gives nothing as held; likely misprinted or misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Not feeling one can run rings round university

clue.text: Poet's sister absorbs as much Pascal as possible

indicators.note: absorbs means the abbreviation for sister takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Pascal's book is the Pensees; as much of that title as will fit leaves PENSE

explanation.surface: A poet's sister reads all of Blaise Pascal she can manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbs' is the container signal. Pascal's Pensees (Thoughts) is cut to fit the space. Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan author of The Faerie Queene, an example of a poet.

clue.text: Part of our duty is making a speech

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Delivering an address is just one of our obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'is making', but the answer is a noun, a language: 'a speech' defines it and 'is making' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech can mean a language or tongue, and Urdu is the language of Pakistan, an example.

clue.text: First two fallers in race

parts.note: the original couple of the human race, who fell from grace in Eden, read as if they were horses falling at a fence

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man and woman ate the forbidden fruit, bringing about the Fall of the human race.

clue.text: Refuse old gondolier

parts.note: marc is the refuse of grapes after pressing

explanation.surface: A Venetian boatman is told to turn down a fare from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse is the noun, waste, not the verb. Marco is one of the two gondolier heroes of Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Palmieri is a gondolier in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta, an example.

clue.text: Expression of disgust about head of foreign kingdom

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes around the initial letter

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone snorts in contempt about the ruler of an overseas realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts F, from 'head of foreign', inside FIE. Fife in Scotland is traditionally called the Kingdom of Fife.
explanation.definitionFit: Fife, the Scottish region, is traditionally known as a kingdom from its days as a Pictish realm.

clue.text: Light verses in books concealing a reality I lost in translation

indicators.note: concealing means the word for bookings holds the rest hidden inside it

parts.note: a referee books a player when giving a caution, so books are cautions

indicators.note: the letter I is lost from the phrase and the rest translated into a new order

explanation.surface: Comic poems appear in volumes that hide a truth garbled by a translator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost in translation' drops the I from 'a reality' and rearranges the rest as ARYTALE; 'concealing' wraps the bookings round it. The book is Hilaire Belloc's comic verse for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Belloc's book of humorous moral poems is a classic of light verse, an example.

clue.text: Appear to lose king in card game

indicators.note: to lose means the king letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to look is to seem or appear
K is the abbreviation for king in cards and chess

explanation.surface: A player seems to lose his king during a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is an old card game; 'to lose' drops K from LOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Loo is a traditional trick-taking card game played for stakes, an example.

clue.text: What feeds duke, and this man?

annotationWithheld.why: What feeds duke, and this man? (6): DINNER looks like D (duke) + INNER (from 'feed the inner man'), but no clue word as held gives INNER; 'this man' gives I or ME
annotationWithheld.clue: What feeds duke, and this man?

clue.text: Big fall in pound — row breaks out

indicators.note: the letters break free and come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Sterling slumps after a quarrel erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big fall' looks financial beside 'pound', but it is heavy rain; POUND and ROW rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a heavy fall of rain, a big fall from the sky.
